title: Quota throttling and charge attribution for interleaved KV prefetch + coalesced batches
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Summary:
Customers and infra teams have reported inconsistent quota throttling and unexpected per-request charges when prefix/KV cache prefetches and on-demand requests are coalesced into a single execution batch. In some multi-tenant flows a subset of requests in a batch were entirely satisfied from KV/prefix cache (0 model tokens) while others executed model tokens; current metering attributes batch-level execution cost incorrectly, causing either overcharging cached requests or under-enforcing quota windows that lead to bursty throttling.
problem_details:
Observed behaviors:
- Cached-prefetch hits sometimes receive non-zero charge because cost is computed at batch granularity and split equally across requests instead of by execution tokens.
- Rate limiter uses 'logical tokens' derived from pre-expansion token estimates rather than actual executed tokens, so quotas are consumed unevenly across tenants.
- Quota windows misalign with batch aggregation heuristics (staggering/async coalescing) causing head-of-line tenants to be throttled while others escape enforcement.
Telemetry snapshots: dashboard://dashboards/gov/metering/batch-attribution shows 0.4% of requests with cached-kv being billed >0 tokens; incidents filed by 2 enterprise customers in last 30d.
proposal:
Design proposal (high level):
1) Separate 'execution_token_count' from 'logical_input_tokens' in the metering pipeline. Execution token = tokens actually processed by runtime (post-KV/prefix cache skip).
2) Compute batch execution cost at runtime and attribute costs to requests proportionally to their executed tokens. Requests with 0 executed tokens should be charged only amortized fixed-invocation cost (configurable small constant) OR free when within free-cache SLA (TBD).
3) Update rate limiter to decrement quota using execution_token_count and maintain a secondary counter for 'prefetch_calls' to allow rate-limiting of prefetch traffic if requested by customers.
4) Introduce 'batch-attribution' hook in serving runtime which emits attribution events (batch_id, request_keys, executed_tokens[], kernel_cost_micros) for accurate offline reconciliation.
5) Migration: dual-write mode where new attribution is recorded in parallel for 2 weeks and reconciled; then switch billing consumer to new pipeline.
6) Add feature flag and tenant-level config for choosing between 'strict-execution' vs 'amortized-equal-split' for backwards compatibility.
acceptance_criteria:
- Billing reports attribute zero model tokens for pure-KV hits (except configured amortized fixed cost).
- Quota counters reflect executed tokens within 1% of runtime-observed execution tokens across 24h sample.
- No increase >5% in tail latency for 95th/99th percentiles after attribution hook enabled.
- End-to-end integration test and synthetic tenant test demonstrating throttling fairness for mixed cached+uncached bursts.
- Migration runbook and reconciliation artifacts produced.
implementation_notes:
Work split:
- Runtime (Ari): batch-attribution hook, compute executed_tokens by request, emit attribution events.
- Metering service (SRE/Marisol): consume attribution events, update consumption model and billing pipeline, implement dual-write reconciliation.
- Rate limiter (Devon): add execution_token decrement path and prefetch counters, expose tenant config.
- Console/Telemetry (Jia): new dashboard panels, alerts for attribution deltas.
Edge cases: partial KV-hit where prefix cache returns partial tokens — ensure executed_tokens reflects only tokens sent to model; ensure tokenization canonicalization between runtime and metering consumer.
Performance: attribution hook must be <200us on hot path; bench expected to add ~0.8% CPU on serving nodes (measured on a small spike).
test_plan:
- Unit tests for attribution math (zero-hit, partial-hit, full-hit).
- Integration test: spawn mixed-ratio synthetic traffic (50% cached, 50% uncached) with coalescing enabled and assert billing records.
- Load test: run 2 hours at peak QPS to measure P95/P99 latency impact and compare token accounting error.
- Reconciliation job: run on historical 72h window comparing old vs new charge and produce diff report.
- Customer sandbox: enable feature for two willing enterprise customers for 10 days and collect feedback.
rollback_plan:
- Feature flag off -> attribution emits stop and metering switches back to old model.
- Reconciliation rollback: billing consumer can choose older aggregated batch-cost table until previous billing cycle closes.
- Communication: notify customers via status.redwood with timeline if billing anomalies detected.
